idea: Root-cause WHY the crews bookkeeper-lead still hits `Denied by preToolUse hook (hook errored)` on nearly every tool call under lock contention, EVEN AFTER the crews 3.23.3 liveness-lock fix made the member-crash sweep fail-soft. Settle which of (2a) the crash-sweep, (2b) a different non-fail-soft lock op, or (2c) the runtime/wrapper error->deny mapping produces the denial, cite file:line proof, and propose a fix that makes the PreToolUse path NEVER hard-deny on a lock/sweep error.
rootCauseVerdict: 2b + 2c (NOT 2a). The crash-sweep is genuinely fail-soft (try/catch at all 4 call sites incl. pre-tool-use.js:475-485) and is NOT the deny source. The deny is produced by a DIFFERENT non-fail-soft lock op on the PreToolUse path -- markArmIntent -> withManifestLock -> acquireLock throwing LockTimeoutError (actors.js:1449-1490, locks.js:171-193), unguarded in handleInput at pre-tool-use.js:490, firing on the lead's listener-arm tool call. That LockTimeoutError is deliberately mapped to a DENY by crews' own FAIL_CLOSED_ERRORS set (pre-tool-use.js:638-641 Claude, copilot-shim.js:204-207 Copilot) AND, if it escapes uncaught/non-zero-exit, by the engine runtime's non-timeout-error->fail-closed deny path (Copilot app.js Pde(t)=x.hookPreToolUseErroredMessage = the literal '(hook errored)' string; the runtime ALLOWS on a hook TIMEOUT but DENIES on any other hook throw). 3.23.3 shrank the lock WINDOW but left the DENIAL mechanism untouched.

candidateDirections.name: PreToolUse fails OPEN on LockTimeoutError (top-level catch-all in handleInput) -- RECOMMENDED
candidateDirections.summary: Wrap the lock-taking region of handleInput (everything after the assertSessionOwnsActor try/catch) in a top-level try/catch; on LockTimeoutError (and any unexpected non-deliberate error) appendLog + return WITHOUT writing a block envelope (= allow). Deliberate blocks are unaffected because they write {decision:block} and return (never throw). Single edit in handleInput covers BOTH engine wrappers and short-circuits before FAIL_CLOSED_ERRORS sees the error. Defense-in-depth: stop treating LockTimeoutError as fail-closed at the two PreToolUse entry points (pre-tool-use.js:638-653 Claude; copilot-pre-tool-use.js:37-48 Copilot, scoped to the PreToolUse shim -- do NOT mutate the shared copilot-shim FAIL_CLOSED_ERRORS used by Stop/SessionStart), and guarantee the wrapper always exits 0 with a valid allow envelope so the runtime '(hook errored)' non-zero-exit path also can't fire. Mirrors the runtime's own 'hook timed out -> proceed' intent. Keep TamperedFileError + the .crews write-guard fail-closed; only the CONTENTION error flips to allow.

candidateDirections.name: Secondary: detect + force-cycle stale pre-fix listeners (NOT required once D1 lands)
candidateDirections.summary: A long-running lib/listener-loop.js process is loaded once at arm time and keeps the OLD O(N)-in-lock sweep until it re-arms (fresh `node $CREWS_BIN arm` on next delivery/timeout); an indefinitely-armed idle listener can stay stale a long time and keeps producing the box-wide AV/IO contention. Optional hardening: stamp the running crews version into the manifest at arm time and have the lead detect + force-cycle (stop+respawn or no-op message to trigger re-arm) members whose listener predates the lock-fix version. This reduces the contention SOURCE but is strictly secondary -- D1 makes the gate resilient regardless. Long-running listeners CANNOT hot-swap code without re-spawn, so 'wait for it to cycle' is unreliable. Best folded into the broader crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention effort.

candidateDirections.name: REJECTED: raise the lock timeout / only further shrink the sweep window
candidateDirections.summary: Raising the 2000ms lock timeout makes the hot path BLOCK longer (toward the 30s hook timeout) -- strictly worse, and the 3.23.3 plan explicitly rejected it. Only further shrinking the sweep window (the 3.23.3/3.19.1 angle) reduces contention FREQUENCY but never changes the fail-closed mapping, so the deny survives any residual contention. Neither addresses the actual denial mechanism.

recommendedDirection: D1-failopen-locktimeout. The load-bearing root cause is the fail-CLOSED mapping of LockTimeoutError on the PreToolUse path (2c), triggered by the unguarded markArmIntent manifest-lock op (2b). The crash-sweep (2a) is already fail-soft and not the cause. Make the PreToolUse path fail-OPEN on LockTimeoutError via a top-level catch-all in handleInput (engine-agnostic, one edit) plus defense-in-depth at both entry points, so lock contention degrades to 'skip the advisory bookkeeping + allow the tool' -- exactly how the engine runtime already treats a hook timeout. This makes the lead resilient to ANY lock contention (including a still-running pre-3.23.3 listener) without depending on cycling offenders. Keep TamperedFileError and the deliberate .crews write-guard fail-closed. D2 (old-listener cycling) is an optional secondary mitigation, not required for correctness. Regression test: force markArmIntent's manifest lock to throw LockTimeoutError on the lead's arm-tool call and assert ALLOW (no deny) -- the case the existing member-crash-lock-contention.test.js (a) does NOT cover (it only forces the sweep to throw); plus a deliberate-block negative case and a wrapper-exits-0 subprocess case.
questionsForSynthesis: Scope of the catch-all: fail-OPEN only on LockTimeoutError (minimal, targeted), or on ANY unexpected non-deliberate throw on the PreToolUse path (broadest resilience)? Recommendation: LockTimeoutError specifically + keep TamperedFileError fail-closed, but a broader 'any non-deliberate throw -> allow' is defensible given the cooperative-agent threat model (PreToolUse is self-discipline, not a security boundary).

Should the LockTimeoutError-allow be scoped to the PreToolUse surface only, or applied to Stop/SessionStart too? The shared copilot-shim.js FAIL_CLOSED_ERRORS set is used by all four Copilot shims; Stop may want different semantics (blocking a stop on lock timeout has the stop_hook_active retry valve). Recommendation: scope to PreToolUse; do not globally mutate the shared set.

Is the operator's literal '(hook errored)' the runtime non-zero-exit/uncaught variant (hookPreToolUseErroredMessage) or a paraphrase of the explicit clean deny 'Denied by preToolUse hook: LockTimeoutError: ...'? Both trace to the same crews root cause; the fix closes both. Worth confirming which variant the operator's crews build produced (does its copilot-pre-tool-use.js catch + emit a deny envelope, or does the throw escape -> non-zero exit?).

Should the old-listener-cycle mitigation (D2) be filed as a separate follow-up task (version-stamp-on-arm + lead force-cycle), or folded into crews-hook-timeout-under-lock-contention which already targets the contention frequency? Recommendation: fold in / defer; D1 alone closes the reported bug.
